newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily coffee report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

Robusta futures in London ended sharply higher on arbitrage buying and trade short-covering. The improved sentiment was also helped by an early rally in New York as the market recovered from Tuesday's slight technical correction.

Keen robusta selling by Vietnam and Indonesia in the past week seemed to have abated as producers held back in view of surging prices, trade sources said. November added $29 per tonne to close at $1,549, while January closed $35 higher at $1,488.

Arabica futures finished firmer with paired gains. Persistent worries about near-term supplies boosted the spot December contract. The premium widened to 7.70 cents/lb with some traders predicting the gap to widen to 10.00 cents/lb. December closed at 113.55 cents/lb, up 1.05 cent/lb, while March added 20 points to close at 105.85 cents/lb. The outer months closed 35 points lower to 25 points higher.
December is expected to remain firm because of a lack of physical coffee available for the US in the next few weeks to help bridge the gap between the two seasons.

BRAZIL - According to FEBEC president Oswaldo Aranha coffee exports in September will probably reach 1.2 million 60-kg bags, slightly below expectations, after a delay in finalising the scrapping of a state export tax. However, exports in October should well be above 1.5 million bags as the month will be somewhat inflated by shipments which were not made in September for technical reasons, he added.

In August it became apparent that the government would approve a bill cutting a 13 per cent state export tax on primary commodities and semi-manufactured goods. However, the necessary documentation was only completed in the middle of September after a period in which exporters held back sales in expectation of its approval.

So far the highest monthly coffee exports this year were seen in August when 1.54 million bags were sold overseas. Under the ACPC retention scheme Brazil can ship 9 million bags in the second half of 1996.

TANZANIA - Tanzania Coffee Board managing director Edward Sannda told Reuters that coffee production in 1996/97 (July/June) could total between 683,000 and 717,000 60-kg bags down from 883,000 bags produced the previous year. The 1996/97 crop is estimated to be worth $90 million down from $139 million last season.

He said the overall quality of Tanzanian coffee was improving and this was reflected in strong demand from Far Eastern and European buyers. A grower education project involving 30 Ministry of Agriculture experts advising smallholders on the latest farming techniques was having a positive impact on improving overall coffee quality, Sannda said.
Yields for coffee production in Tanzania are among the lowest in the world, averaging 200-300 kg per ha, due mostly to the age of the coffee trees, in some areas more than 100 years old.

COLOMBIA - The Colombian government held a high-level security meeting on October 8 to discuss ways of curbing a recent surge in leftist guerilla activity across the country. But the meeting ended with no specific announcements about possible ways of cracking down on Colombia's newly emboldened rebels.
Guerillas took more than 60 soldiers prisoner, blew up oil pipelines and paralyzed key road ways burning trucks and blocking exports of coffee in a spiral of attacks.

UNITED STATES - The United States imported 1.460 million bags of coffee in July 1996 nearly 20 per cent more than was imported the same month the previous year. That brought total imports since the beginning of 1996 up to 11.521 million bags, 16 per cent more than was imported the same period in 1995. Total imports in calendar year 1995 rose to 17.1 million bags up from 16.2 million bags imported in 1994.

Major suppliers of green coffee in January/July 1996 were Guatemala (1.069 vs 1.008 million bags), Mexico (2.963 vs 2.083 million bags), Colombia (1.649 vs 1.299 million bags) and Vietnam (807 800 vs 456 200 bags).

The country exported 1.165 million bags of coffee in January/July 1996 25 per cent more than was exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in calendar year 1995 dropped by 22 per cent to 1.841 million bags.
